title: Civic belonging and practical support can function as political capacity
source_unit: CIRCLE 2026 Political Homes research on youth civic access, belonging, support, and participation
geography: United States; young people and youth civic-engagement contexts

denominator.unit: reported CIRCLE youth research sample; exact denominator not used in this extraction

civic_action_difference.value: young people with access to political homes demonstrated civic action about 20 percentage points higher than peers without that access

civic_self_efficacy_difference.value: young people with access to political homes also showed higher civic self-efficacy by about 20 percentage points

political_home_resources.value: political homes can provide safe third spaces, belonging, civic information, food, financial compensation, and transportation to youth

wellbeing_buffer.value: strong political-home connections were reported to buffer mental-health costs associated with political involvement

observations.method: Review of CIRCLE's 2026 Political Homes analysis; civic action, self-efficacy, belonging, practical support, and wellbeing are retained as separate reported surfaces.
observations.uncertainty: The public analysis is not a randomized assignment to a political home and does not establish that the support setting caused civic action. Exact sample construction, measure wording, subgroup denominators, and the timing of support relative to action must be preserved from the underlying study materials.
observations.subgroup: Young people with and without reported access to political-home settings; the public summary highlights historically marginalized and underserved youth but does not supply all subgroup estimates in the page extraction.
observations.counterinterpretation: Youth who already have more time, safety, social connection, resources, or political interest may be more likely both to enter a political home and to participate. A supportive space may also enable action for some people while imposing emotional, time, or identity costs for others.

related_sources.claim: CIRCLE's 2026 report provides the political-home framework and the relationship between civic belonging, practical support, civic self-efficacy, action, and wellbeing.
CIRCLE's toolkit supplies the applied political-home and youth-support framework; it is not treated as an outcome estimate.

boundary: This record supports a bounded social-infrastructure-to-civic-capacity association. It does not establish a causal effect of political homes, final turnout, policy influence, institutional response, durable trust, or a same-person route from material support to political action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official CIRCLE HTML research page retrieved and hashed; underlying respondent data and full analytic files not retained
